mechanism_narrative: A sustained 20-day decline in the federal funds rate signals an easing monetary policy cycle, compressing discount rates on equity cash flows and generating positive S&P 500 forward returns.
failure_condition: SPX produces negative 20-day returns despite a sustained 20-day decline in FEDFUNDS within the same period.

mechanism_narrative: A crossing of the federal funds rate above 2% triggers a negative S&P 500 forward return over the next 5 trading days due to heightened inflation expectations.
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 5-day returns despite FEDFUNDS crossing above 2% in the same period.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained 60-day increase in GDP demand (GDPC1) predicts positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next quarter as expanded economic activity boosts corporate earnings growth.
failure_condition: SPX produces negative 60-day returns despite a sustained 60-day increase in GDPC1 within the same period.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained 20-day rise in the industrial production index (INDPRO) indicates strengthening supply chains, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns as production efficiency improves.
failure_condition: SPX produces negative 20-day returns despite a sustained 20-day increase in INDPRO within the same period.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained 5-day decline in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) signals labor market strengthening, driving positive S&P 500 forward returns as investor confidence in economic growth rises.
failure_condition: SPX produces negative 5-day returns despite a sustained 5-day decline in UNRATE within the same period.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained 20-day increase in nonfarm payrolls (PAYEMS) predicts positive S&P 500 forward returns as expanded employment signals robust economic growth and corporate stability.
failure_condition: SPX produces negative 20-day returns despite a sustained 20-day increase in PAYEMS within the same period.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous decline in the federal funds rate below 2% and a sustained drop in unemployment (UNRATE below 3%) over 20 days creates a dual accommodative signal, driving positive S&P 500 forward returns through reduced financing costs and labor market expansion.
failure_condition: SPX produces negative 20-day returns despite both FEDFUNDS < 2% and UNRATE < 3% occurring within the same period.

mechanism_narrative: During a monetary tightening cycle, a sustained 60-day rise in the federal funds rate predicts negative S&P 500 forward returns as higher interest rates compress equity valuations and raise borrowing costs.
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 60-day returns despite a sustained 60-day rise in FEDFUNDS within the same period during an active tightening cycle.
